Under MIDH, 50% subsidy: anti-bird or anti-hail nets Rs.50 per sq.m (subsidy Rs.25), up to 10,000 sq.m; their permanent support structure Rs.20 per sq.m (Rs.10), up to 2 ha; fencing Rs.300 per running metre (Rs.150), up to 1,000 m, only with another MIDH component; fruit or bunch covers Rs.50,000 per ha (Rs.25,000), up to 2 ha; vegetable support system Rs.20,000 per ha (Rs.10,000), up to 2 ha.

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH individual farm pond subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. Individual farm pond for horticulture under MIDH: standard size 20m x 20m x 3m (1,200 cu.m), unit cost Rs.1.50 lakh; subsidy 50%, which is Rs.75,000, worked at Rs.62.50 per cu.m of actual volume, including 300 micron plastic or RCC lining. Unlined ponds (black cotton soil only) cost 30% less. Smaller ponds pro rata. Released after completion with fencing and sign board, on joint inspection; complete within 60 days of sanction. Existing RCC-lined and old incomplete ponds are not eligible.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH community water harvesting tank subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH new orchard area expansion subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. New orchards (area expansion) under MIDH: up to 40% of the total cost of plant material, inputs, supports and INM/IPM, paid over two years in a 60:40 ratio. The second year is paid only if at least 80% of plants survive. Paid by DBT. Land must be certified from the pattadar passbook or adangal. Per-hectare unit costs differ by crop and spacing.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

text: Andhra Pradesh. Mushroom under MIDH: small mushroom production unit of 200 sq.ft, cost norm Rs.2 lakh, 50% assistance, up to 5 units per beneficiary, bank loan not needed. Larger production, spawn or compost units (Rs.20 to 30 lakh): 40% credit-linked back-ended subsidy for the private sector.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH farm gate pack house and cold room subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. Farm gate pack house (9m x 6m) under MIDH: unit cost limited to Rs.4.80 lakh, 50% assistance. Add-on farm gate cold room up to 10 MT: 35% of unit cost, unit cost limited to Rs.20 lakh (solar with battery), Rs.8 lakh (thermal storage on grid), Rs.12 lakh (biomass) or Rs.5 lakh (conventional grid). Land must be owned or on a registered lease of at least 10 years.

subject: Andhra Pradesh paddy procurement rules KMS 2026-27
text: Andhra Pradesh. Paddy procurement, Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27 (Kharif and Rabi): MSP for FAQ paddy Rs.2,441 per quintal common, Rs.2,461 Grade A. Procured only from farmers (tenants included) registered in e-Panta through the Rythu Seva Kendram, at procurement centres in the RSKs; payment Aadhaar-based from e-Panta data. FAQ paddy moisture up to 17%; paddy not meeting FAQ is to be dried and cleaned, not refused outright. The farmer may choose the rice mill, but transport is paid at the lowest slab in the area and beyond 40 km is not paid. Millers buying privately must pay at least MSP into the farmer's bank account.

subject: Tamil Nadu CM Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam farmer welfare benefits
text: Tamil Nadu. Chief Minister's Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam: for agricultural labourers (including fisheries, dairy, horticulture, sericulture, cattle, poultry, plantation work) and small or marginal farmers owning up to 2.5 acres wet or 5 acres dry land who farm directly, cultivating tenants included, aged 18 to 65. Benefits for the member: marriage assistance Rs.8,000 (male) or Rs.10,000 (female); old age pension Rs.1,200 a month; Rs.1,000 a month while incapacitated by TB, cancer, HIV, dialysis, fractures and other listed illnesses; accident death Rs.1 lakh (landless labourers Rs.2 lakh), injury Rs.20,000 to Rs.1 lakh; natural death Rs.20,000 (landless Rs.30,000); funeral Rs.2,500 (landless Rs.10,000); paralysis Rs.50,000. Dependants: education help Rs.1,250 to Rs.6,750 a year, marriage assistance as above.

subject: Tamil Nadu Agricultural Engineering Department machinery hire charges
text: Tamil Nadu. Agricultural Engineering Department machinery hired to farmers, 2026-27, per hour including diesel: bulldozer Rs.1,230; tractor Rs.500; mini tractor Rs.460; paddy combine harvester wheel type Rs.1,160, track type Rs.1,880; backhoe with front-end loader (JCB type) Rs.890; mini backhoe Rs.650; crawler excavator Rs.1,910; sugarcane harvester with infielders Rs.5,120; truck coconut hoist Rs.450; tractor with implements, pumpset or paddy mobile dryer Rs.500 (dryer burner fuel and labour extra); heavy chain saw Rs.85 (fuel and labour extra). Minor irrigation machinery: rotary drill Rs.130 per metre, percussion drill Rs.300 a day, mini drill Rs.70 per metre, hand boring set Rs.30 per metre, rock blasting Rs.250 per blast, resistivity meter Rs.500 per point, electrical logger Rs.1,000 per bore hole; for these the farmer pays diesel, labour, pipes, pebbles and transport. Machinery goes to farmers who pay in advance; book on e-Vaadagai 2.0 in the Uzhavar App, or ask the block Assistant Engineer or Junior Engineer of the Agricultural Engineering Department. For private hirers and contractors, a 2022 order (G.O.(Ms).No.61 of 15.03.2022) set higher rates: excavator Rs.2,400, backhoe Rs.1,250, bulldozer Rs.1,550; any later revision of those is not held.

Wheat free in place of rice, up to 10 kg in Chennai and district headquarters and 5 kg elsewhere. Sugar 500 g per person, up to 2 kg, at Rs.13.50 a kg for AAY and Rs.25 for others; sugar-option cards get 3 kg more in place of rice. Tur dal 1 kg at Rs.30. Palmolein 1 litre at Rs.25. SC and ST farmers with rainfed land and no irrigation: a borewell or tubewell with an electric motor or solar pumpset at 100% subsidy, up to Rs.8 lakh per farmer, for 300 farmers in 2026-27. subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH horticulture machinery subsidy

Tractor up to 20 PTO HP: 2WD cost Rs.4 lakh, subsidy up to Rs.2 lakh (others Rs.1.60 lakh); 4WD cost Rs.4.90 lakh, up to Rs.2.45 lakh (others Rs.1.96 lakh). Power tiller 8 to 11 BHP: cost Rs.2 lakh, up to Rs.1 lakh (others Rs.80,000); above 11 BHP: cost Rs.2.40 lakh, up to Rs.1.20 lakh (others Rs.1 lakh). Powered knapsack or Taiwan sprayer above 16 litres: cost Rs.20,000, up to Rs.10,000 (others Rs.8,000). Tractor boom sprayer: cost Rs.82,000, up to Rs.41,000 (others Rs.33,000). Tractor air-assisted sprayer: cost Rs.2.76 lakh, up to Rs.1.38 lakh (others Rs.1.10 lakh). Electrostatic sprayer: cost Rs.5 lakh, up to Rs.2.50 lakh (others Rs.2 lakh). subject: Tamil Nadu oil palm subsidy NMEO-OP 2026-27

Oil palm (NMEO-OP), 2026-27: planting material subsidy Rs.20,000 per ha for indigenous and Rs.29,000 per ha for imported seedlings (150 seedlings per ha), supplied through the allotted oil palm firm. During the 4-year gestation period, 50% of maintenance cost up to Rs.5,250 per ha a year and 50% of intercrop inputs up to Rs.5,250 per ha a year, Rs.42,000 per ha in all. Tools at 50% up to: oil palm cutter Rs.2,500, protective wire mesh Rs.20,000, motorised chisel Rs.15,000, aluminium ladder Rs.5,000, chaff cutter Rs.50,000, tractor trolley Rs.2 lakh. Production incentive Rs.1,000 per tonne of fresh fruit bunches above 8 tonnes per ha from plantations 5 years or older. Register on TNHORTNET.

text: Andhra Pradesh. Subsidy seeds under the various schemes are given at the Rythu Seva Kendram through the D-Krishi app: the RSK in-charge identifies the farmer, who is authenticated by biometrics, face recognition or an OTP to the Aadhaar-linked mobile, both when paying the non-subsidy share and when taking the seed; a message with the registration ID goes to that mobile. Allocation runs state to district to mandal to RSK, and AP Seeds supplies RSKs directly. The subsidy rate for each crop is not in this order.

subject: Andhra Pradesh fishing ban relief eligibility
text: Andhra Pradesh, Marine Fishing Ban Relief, who can get it (G.O.Rt.No.139 of 22.04.2025). Crew of mechanized, motorized and traditional crafts registered under the M.S. Act 1958 on or before 14 April of the year, with a valid APMFR Act 1995 licence for the current Fasli year. Boats under the HSD oil subsidy must have drawn at least 1,000 litres (mechanized) or 100 litres (motorized) in the previous year; all sea-going boats qualify whatever their HSD drawal. Not eligible: those covered by another government DBT scheme or by the NTR Bharosa fishermen pension; family income above Rs.1.20 lakh (rural) or Rs.1.44 lakh (urban) a year; land above 3 acres wet or 10 acres dry or 10 acres together; a family four-wheeler (taxi, tractor, auto exempt); electricity use above 300 units a month; in municipal areas, a house site of 1,000 sq.ft or more; a family member in government service, drawing a government pension, or paying income tax. Six-step validation applies.

subject: Tamil Nadu price support scheme pulses and copra quality norms

subject: Tamil Nadu PM-KISAN eligibility as published by Tamil Nadu
text: Tamil Nadu. PM-KISAN: Rs.6,000 a year in three instalments of Rs.2,000 by DBT to land-holding farm families. Not eligible: land acquired after 1.2.2019, institutional landholders, families with a present or former constitutional post holder, minister, MP, MLA, mayor or district panchayat chair, serving or retired government or PSU employees (except Group D), pensioners drawing Rs.10,000 a month or more, income tax payers in at least three of the last five assessment years (two of them consecutive), practising doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects, and NRIs. Every year: annual e-KYC in April, land records linked, Aadhaar-seeded bank account and Farmer ID registered on the PM-KISAN portal.

subject: Tamil Nadu seed selling licence, testing and certification fees
text: Tamil Nadu. Seed sample testing (purity, germination, moisture): Rs.80 a sample at government seed testing labs; ISTA orange certificate Rs.4,000, blue certificate Rs.2,000. Seed certification: application Rs.25, then field inspection per 0.40 ha, for example variety paddy Rs.100, hybrid paddy Rs.250, pulses Rs.80. Seed processing unit approval Rs.4,000 for three years. PGS organic and natural farming certification is free for farmers.

subject: Andhra Pradesh agricultural market fee
text: Andhra Pradesh. Under the Andhra Pradesh (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966, agricultural market committees collect market fee at 1% ad valorem from the purchaser of notified produce and livestock bought in the notified market area. Produce on which fee was paid and that is later exported out of the state is exempt from a second levy on proof of payment (section 12(1-A)). subject: Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivator Rights Card (CCRC) for tenant farmers
text: Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 (Act 30 of 2019). A tenant (cultivator) and land owner sign an agreement in the form of a Crop Cultivator Rights Card for 11 months, countersigned by the Village Revenue Officer at the Village Secretariat, who must issue it within 3 days, with a copy to the owner. With the card the cultivator gets undisturbed possession for the period even if the land is sold, crop loans from banks and cooperatives (the bank may not ask for other documents and may not attach the land for the cultivator's dues), crop insurance, crop damage relief and other government benefits; SC, ST, BC and minority cultivators also get Rythu Bharosa. The owner keeps ownership, revenue records are not changed, the owner can end the agreement only if the terms are broken, with two months' written notice, and can take loans other than crop loans on the land. The cultivator must vacate at the end, use the land only for farming and repay the crop loan after harvest. Appeals: Tahsildar, then Sub-Collector or RDO, then Joint Collector, each within 7 days. Government land and land assigned to the poor are excluded. Read from a scanned gazette copy. The Act comes into force on a date the government notifies; that notification is not held.

subject: Andhra Pradesh compensation for crop damage, cattle death and human death or injury by wild animals
text: Andhra Pradesh, compensation for damage by tigers and other wild animals (G.O.Ms.No.29 of 22.07.2024, in force at once). Human death: Rs.10 lakh ex gratia (was Rs.5 lakh). Grievous injury: Rs.2 lakh plus medical expenses. Minor injury: actual cost of treatment or Rs.20,000, whichever is lower. Cattle killed: a value to be decided and notified with the Director of Animal Husbandry. Crops, per acre: paddy Rs.10,000; sugarcane Rs.12,000; other crops Rs.10,000. Mango and coconut trees: Rs.2,000 per tree. Horticulture crops such as banana and citrus: loss up to Rs.12,000 per acre paid in full; loss of Rs.12,000 to Rs.35,000 paid at 50%, at least Rs.12,000 and at most Rs.24,000 per acre; loss above Rs.35,000 paid at 30%, at least Rs.24,000 and at most Rs.50,000 per acre, as assessed by a team of Revenue and Horticulture officers. Paid to the head of the family on a certificate from the Revenue authorities, through the Forest Department.

subject: Andhra Pradesh concessional power tariff for aquaculture farms
text: Andhra Pradesh. Power for aquaculture farms at a concessional Rs.1.50 per unit (the rest is paid by the Fisheries Department): for farms up to 10 acres in notified aquaculture development zones (G.O.Rt.No.92 of 2022); from 1 June 2026 also for eligible farms in newly declared aqua zones and all farms registered under the APSADA Act or CAA Act, and future registrations from their registration date. The farm must achieve a power factor of 0.9 to 0.95 by March 2027 or lose the subsidy. An earlier order set Rs.3.85 per unit for farms above 5 acres; whether that still applies above 10 acres is not stated.

subject: Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF): who runs it and how to join
text: Andhra Pradesh. Natural farming is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS), a not-for-profit body of the Agriculture Department, as APCNF since 2016, and RySS is the State Natural Farming Cell for the National Mission on Natural Farming (G.O.Ms.No.5, Agri & Coop, 09.02.2025). In each district a District Project Manager of RySS implements it; at mandal level, RySS mandal anchors and senior natural farming community resource persons work under a committee chaired by the Block Development Officer, with the Mandal Agriculture Officer. In 2024, 10.37 lakh farm families covering 4.86 lakh ha in all 658 rural mandals were in the programme, with about 2,000 village bio-input shops. Payments per acre to natural farmers in AP are not in these documents.

subject: Andhra Pradesh conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural use (NALA repeal)
text: Andhra Pradesh. The Agricultural Land (Conversion for Non-Agricultural Purposes) Act, 2006 (the NALA Act, with its conversion tax) is repealed with effect from 3 September 2025, first by Ordinance No.5 of 2025 and then by L.A. Bill No.29 of 2025, introduced on 26 September 2025. Land use is now regulated by local bodies and urban development authorities under their own laws, such as the AP Metropolitan Region and Urban Development Authorities Act, 2016, which levy development charges. Applications pending under the old Act are decided under it, and conversion tax already assessed can still be recovered. Unauthorised layouts are treated as validly converted on payment of conversion tax on the basic value of their period, with no penalty or interest, for one year from commencement. Whether the Bill has passed is not held.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Land (Conversion for Non Agricultural Purposes) (Repeal) Bill, 2025, L.A. Bill No.29 of 2025, A.P. Gazette Part IV-A Extraordinary No.29 Dt.26.09.2025, copy hosted by PRS

subject: Tamil Nadu tenant farmer laws and Revenue Courts
text: Tamil Nadu. Disputes between land owners and cultivating tenants are heard by 10 Revenue Courts, each presided over by a Special Deputy Collector with quasi-judicial powers, at Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Tiruvarur, Thanjavur, Mannargudi, Tiruchirappalli, Lalgudi, Nagapattinam, Madurai and Tirunelveli. They apply the Cultivating Tenants Protection Act, 1955; the Cultivating Tenants (Payment of Fair Rent) Act, 1956; the Public Trusts (Regulation and Administration of Agricultural Land) Act, 1961; and the Agricultural Lands (Record of Tenancy Rights) Act, 1969. Cultivating tenants can also join the CM Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam and the crop insurance scheme. Land ceiling: 30 standard acres for a family of five (Land Reforms Act). The fair rent rates themselves are not held.

source.doc: Tamil Nadu Revenue and Disaster Management Department Policy Note 2026-27, sections 5.1 and 5.2

subject: Tamil Nadu Uzhavar Sandhai farmers' markets

Uzhavar Sandhai (farmers' markets): fruit and vegetable growers holding an identity card from the Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business sell directly to consumers; shops and weighing balances are given free, first come first served, and cold storage at some Uzhavar Sandhais is free. Contact the Deputy Director of Agriculture (Agri Business) or the Uzhavar Sandhai Administrative Officer. Regulated markets offer storage godowns, drying yards and same-day price settlement to all farmers.

subject: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Infrastructure Fund loans

Agriculture Infrastructure Fund: loans for post-harvest management and farm infrastructure for farmers, FPOs, SHGs, agri-entrepreneurs and primary cooperative credit societies, with 3% interest subvention and credit guarantee on loans up to Rs.2 crore, repayable within 7 years; the bank decides eligibility and should decide within 2 months. subject: Andhra Pradesh PMFBY: end of free insurance, voluntary enrolment, how claims are settled
text: Andhra Pradesh crop insurance (PMFBY, yield based, G.O.Ms.No.80, 04.09.2024): free coverage based on e-Panta was given only in Kharif 2024; from Rabi 2024-25 enrolment is voluntary (the scheme was extended to 2026-27 on a voluntary basis by G.O.Ms.No.34 of 06.07.2026). subject: Tamil Nadu revenue certificates online through e-Sevai
text: Tamil Nadu. Revenue certificates are applied for online through e-Sevai (Revenue Department with TNeGA), including: community, income, nativity, first graduate, deserted women, agriculture income, inter-caste marriage, widow, unemployment, family migration, small or marginal farmer, loss of educational records in disasters, unmarried, no male child, legal heir, residency, OBC, EWS (income and assets), destitute widow, Jain religious minority and BC Muslim certificates, and pawn broker, money lender, public building and temporary cracker licences. Unmarried and unemployment certificates use self-declaration with Aadhaar-based verification. Mass contact programmes are held in every district on the second Wednesday of each month. Fees and time limits are not in this document.

subject: Andhra Pradesh milk procurement: fair testing and complaints by dairy farmers
text: Andhra Pradesh Milk Procurement (Protection of Farmers) and Enforcement of Safety of Milk Standards Act, 2023 and Rules (G.O.Ms.No.02, AHDD&F, 10.01.2024). Milk collection centres and dairies may use only licensed milk analysers, verified by the Milk Inspector; a standard analyser must read fat and SNF within plus or minus 0.2 of the reference method. The farmer is given an acknowledgement card or book showing the type of milk (buffalo or cow), quantity, fat %, SNF %, rate per litre and amount. If the amount paid is less than the receipt or card shows, the farmer can complain to the Milk Inspector of the village and mandal on the prescribed form. Any aggrieved person can also complain to a magistrate. Appeals under the Act cost Rs.500. Read from a scanned copy.

source.doc: G.O.Ms.No.02 AHDD&F (AH.III) Dt.10.01.2024 - AP Milk Procurement (Protection of Farmers) and Enforcement of Safety of Milk Standards Rules, 2023

subject: Tamil Nadu change of land use from agriculture to non-agriculture
text: Tamil Nadu. Converting agricultural land to non-agricultural use in non-planning areas is governed by the Tamil Nadu Change of Land Use (From Agriculture to Non-agriculture Purposes in Non-planning Areas) Rules, 2017, under the Town and Country Planning Act, 1971: the applicant uploads documents and the Director of Town and Country Planning gives prior concurrence. From the amendment of 31 July 2026 (G.O. Ms. No.149, Housing and Urban Development, published 3 August 2026), for dry land the Director decides the prior concurrence himself on the uploaded documents. The fees, the full document list and the rules for wet land and planning areas are not held.
